own_scenes.desc: Un invento de los medios desde 1997 para meter en el mismo saco disco reciclado, groove analógico minimalista, hip hop instrumental, synth-pop y drum ’n’ bass, presentado como el relevo de un rock estancado. La industria estadounidense se fijó en el techno cuando Astralwerks (rama semiautónoma de Virgin) publicó Exit Planet Dust de los Chemical Brothers (1995); Dig Your Own Hole fue disco de oro y «Block Rockin’ Beats» ganó el Grammy al mejor instrumental de rock. Maverick, el sello de Madonna, fichó a The Prodigy, y tras ellos llegaron Underworld, Propellerheads, Portishead o Fatboy Slim: casi todos con guitarras sampleadas y breakbeats que anclaban lo «nuevo» al rock y al hip hop que el público ya conocía. El programa Amp de MTV (1997-2001), sin presentador, el festival Organic, el cine (Trainspotting, Pi, The Saint de Orbital) y los anuncios (Dirty Vegas, Model 500 para Ford, Matthew Dear, Dabrye) acostumbraron a Estados Unidos al sonido, pero sin contexto: como con el grunge, la prensa resumió décadas en un par de nombres. Para Peter Wohelski (Astralwerks, luego Beatport) la música acabó aceptada por ósmosis, gracias a internet, Ableton Live y Reason, y no por ningún disco ni vídeo.

notes.chapter: Cap. 6: Applied Technology: The Myth of Techno Collides with Reality, 1991–2001
notes.text: Prodigy, por lejos que esté del techno, es uno de los mayores éxitos de la música de baile electrónica: The Fat of the Land fue platino enseguida.

influences.name: Acid house y rave en Gran Bretaña

refs.q: A convenient media contrivance, “electronica” was concocted to encompass styles as varied as reconfigured disco, minimal and abstracted analog grooves, instrumental hip-hop, melodic synth-pop, the splintered rhythms of “drum ’n’ bass”—just about everything that wears the badge of electronic production on its sleeve.
refs.para: A convenient media contrivance, “electronica” was concocted to encompass styles as varied as reconfigured disco, minimal and abstracted analog grooves, instrumental hip-hop, melodic synth-pop, the splintered rhythms of “drum ’n’ bass”—just about everything that wears the badge of electronic production on its sleeve. While “electronica” works well for categorizing, marketing, and cashing in on the general electronic phenomenon, it precludes any true understanding of the music’s details, anecdotes, and minutiae. Each individual style suffers under the electronica umbrella, but none more than techno, the genre that has had the most impact worldwide and has the largest story to tell.
refs.chapter: Cap. 1: Welcome to the Machine: America Wakes Up to Techno, 1997–2010

refs.q: He said, ‘They would be so much cooler if they had a drummer.’”
refs.para: This reliance on traditional rock band sounds is not difficult to understand—forty-odd years of rock ’n’ roll have left a power-ballad patina on the music industry’s minds and business practices. As Wohelski recalls, “The Chemical Brothers were coming on tour, and someone who was an artist manager on the West Coast . . . sat down with me and my partner. He thought the Chemicals were amazing and wanted them to do a remix for a group that he also managed. He said, ‘They would be so much cooler if they had a drummer.’”
refs.chapter: Cap. 1: Welcome to the Machine: America Wakes Up to Techno, 1997–2010

refs.q: Success seems to have come more through osmosis than through any one record or music video.
refs.para: Looking back, it’s impossible to tell if the heightened media awareness of electronica in the late 1990s got techno where it is today, or if much of this has happened covertly in its global subculture. The hope was that the music would become as assimilated into American culture as it is in every other corner of the world. The truth is a lot more complicated and remains long after the promise of the electronica marketing push has faded. Success seems to have come more through osmosis than through any one record or music video. Even the electronic music magazine XLR8R suggests that the concept, if not the genre itself, has outlived its usefulness: “this is where the media broke the ground for electronica’s early grave—the second some know-it-all critic gave a stack of dance music niches one homogenous name.”
refs.chapter: Cap. 1: Welcome to the Machine: America Wakes Up to Techno, 1997–2010

similar_scenes.name: Eurodisco electrónica
similar_scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
similar_scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
similar_scenes.desc: El hit de Donna Summer «I Feel Love», hecho con sonidos sintéticos por Giorgio Moroder, italiano residente en Múnich: junto al synth pop de Kraftwerk, una refulgente visión de Europa orientada al futuro. Será la base del synthpop y de la «disco pervertida» del postpunk.
similar_scenes.family: Ritmos negros: dub, funk, disco y hip hop

similar_scenes.name: Electrónica casera: The Normal y Mute
similar_scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
similar_scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
similar_scenes.desc: Contagiado por las Desperate Bicycles, Daniel Miller compra un Korg usado y graba en su cuarto «T.V.O.D.»/«Warm Leatherette» como The Normal: electropunk de puñaladas de sintetizador y erotismo de accidentes de coche a lo Crash de Ballard. Vende treinta mil copias y le convierte en director de Mute (Fad Gadget). A mediados de 1978 coinciden otros singles electrónicos lo-fi de sellos indie: «United» de Throbbing Gristle, Extended Play de Cabaret Voltaire, «Being Boiled» de The Human League, «Paralysis» de Robert Rental y «Private Plane» de Thomas Leer, hecho sin sintetizador y susurrado para no despertar a su novia.

similar_scenes.name: Electrónica de los setenta
similar_scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
similar_scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
similar_scenes.desc: La primera dosis de electrónica extrema para los chicos de Sheffield fue la banda sonora de Walter Carlos para La naranja mecánica; antes solo había atisbos en el Moog de Keith Emerson y los chorros de ruido de Eno en Roxy Music. Detrás asoman la música concreta, Morton Subotnick y los paisajes de Tangerine Dream.
similar_scenes.family: Antecedentes: punk, art rock, kraut y glam

similar_scenes.name: Electrónica y rock
similar_scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
similar_scenes.desc: El sintetizador de Robert Moog (1966) revoluciona el rock hasta la última fibra. La vanguardia lo adopta primero (Morton Subotnick); después llegan Mort Garson, Ron Geesin, Walter Carlos (Switched On Bach, primer disco electrónico en las listas; Sonic Seasonings anticipa el ambient), Lothar & The Hand People, Silver Apples (dúo de teclados electrónicos que se adelanta una década a la new wave y el synth-pop), Beaver & Krause, David Borden, Bo Hansson y Tonto's Expanding Head Band. El Minimoog portátil (1970) lleva el sintetizador a los escenarios.

similar_scenes.name: Vanguardia: minimalismo y electrónica en vivo
similar_scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
similar_scenes.desc: De las escuelas de vanguardia, la más relevante para el rock fue el minimalismo. La Monte Young y su Theater Of Eternal Music (Tony Conrad, John Cale, Jon Hassell, Terry Riley) crean una música de ondas semiestacionarias; Terry Riley la populariza con «In C» y «A Rainbow In Curved Air»; Steve Reich es el maestro de la repetición; Philip Glass se acerca a la música popular. En la electrónica en vivo: Morton Subotnick, Tod Dockstader, Musica Elettronica Viva, Gordon Mumma, Alvin Lucier, Phill Niblock y la composición por ordenador.

similar_scenes.name: Post-rock: Tortoise y la electrónica del indie
similar_scenes.book: Techno Rebels: The Renegades of Electronic Funk
similar_scenes.author: Dan Sicko
similar_scenes.desc: Otra salida para la evolución del techno, mal nombrada: una extensión de las estructuras del rock con apariencia de banda. Míchigan es uno de sus centros (His Name Is Alive, de Livonia, en 4AD; Windy & Carl), aunque apenas ha conectado con el techno de Detroit. Tortoise, formado en Chicago en 1990 por miembros de una docena de bandas y anclado en el batería John McEntire, renunció a guitarras y voces: en directo, vibráfonos, marimbas, guitarras de pedal, sintetizadores y cajas de ritmos para una mezcla de música de baile desenrollada, dub y bandas sonoras, con temas que migran de un proyecto a otro («Jetty», de «La Jetee» de Isotope 217). El indie acabó abrazando la electrónica: Postal Service, Four Tet, Caribou, Broadcast.

similar_scenes.name: Electrónica para cine, radio y dibujos
similar_scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
similar_scenes.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
similar_scenes.desc: Pioneros con una visión «mucho menos intelectualizada» que la de sus homólogos europeos, que normalizan el sonido electrónico a través del cine, la televisión, la publicidad y los dibujos animados.

similar_scenes.name: Psicodelia electrónica
similar_scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
similar_scenes.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
similar_scenes.desc: Las bandas bañadas en psicodelia tantean el sintetizador y los osciladores como procesadores de sonido. Silver Apples, dúo de oscilador casero («The Simeon») y batería, pasó por el tamiz electrónico el blues, el folk y el pop psicodélico, e incluso sampleó la radio antes que Holger Czukay.

similar_scenes.name: Electrónica naif
similar_scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
similar_scenes.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
similar_scenes.desc: Electrónica de melodías como «nanas para niños adictos a Internet». Mouse on Mars quisieron que la música entrara en el oyente y no solo lo rodeara; de ahí una electrónica de experimentación sencilla y canciones de cuna (Sonig, Plone, Ensemble). Cumbres: Leila y, sobre todo, Boards of Canada, cuyo Music Has the Right to Children evoca recuerdos de infancia.

similar_scenes.name: Leftfield (electrónica experimental post-rave)
similar_scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
similar_scenes.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
similar_scenes.desc: La experimental de los noventa fue post-rave y post-digital: veteranos del industrial y desertores del techno ensanchan la tierra de nadie entre lo culto y lo popular, donde conviven dance, noise, drones, ambient, improvisación, electroacústica y computer music. La prensa lo llamó «leftfield»: no un sonido, sino una perspectiva heterodoxa capaz de apreciar a la vez a Gottfried Michael Koenig, los dubs de King Tubby y la marcialidad de Surgeon. Psychic TV, Chris & Cosey y Coil abrazan el acid.

similar_scenes.name: Trap español y electrónica latina
similar_scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
similar_scenes.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
similar_scenes.desc: Subgénero del sur de EE UU (rimas en tríadas, TR-808, textura gótica) que en España encarnan Pxxr Gvng, Yung Beef, Kinder Malo, Pimp Flaco, Dellafuente o Cecilio G.: más vídeos de YouTube que discos. «No existe tanta diferencia entre un aficionado al trap y un fiestero de la Ruta del bakalao.» A su lado, el dancehall de Bad Gyal, el reggaetón experimental de Miss Nina o La Favi y el electrolatino de Juan Magán.
similar_scenes.family: Hip hop, breaks y ritmo lento

podcast.title: Year Zero (1988) in the UK
podcast.body: The year 1988 is considered "Year Zero" for Electronica, particularly in the UK. This was when Detroit Techno, Chicago House, and the New York dance scene were enthusiastically embraced by English music fans, coinciding with the "Summer of Love" and the rise of ecstasy, which catalyzed a new dance and rave culture. "This brings us to Year Zero in the whole history of what we now call Electronica."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Third Choice in 2000
podcast.body: In 2000, electronica was presented as a "third choice" for music listeners, after pop, rap, and hip hop, suggesting its growing popularity. "A third choice would be all the flavors of electronica."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 14

podcast.title: Broad and Meaningless Term
podcast.body: Electronica was described as a term used in the late 90s that was "so broad that it's almost meaningless," encompassing a wave of bands that seemed to eschew guitars entirely. "There's one more genre that I want to highlight and I hesitate ever so slightly. Because it's a term that's so broad that it's almost meaningless."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Component of Trip Hop
podcast.body: Electronica was identified as one of the genres that crossbred with hip hop to create Trip Hop. "Trip Hop, a British crossbreeding of hip hop and electronica."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Decline (Early 2000s)
podcast.body: At the start of the new century, the music scene began to move away from electronica. "At the start of the new century, we began to move away from electronica new metal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Diverse Applications
podcast.body: The term Electronica was applied to a wide range of artists, including Underworld, The Crystal Method, Faithless, Moby (for non-danceable headphone music), and even parts of Madonna's *Ray of Light*, U2's *Pop*, and anything Björk did in the 1990s. "Underworld and the Crystal Method and Faithless were definitely Electronica. Some people called what Fat Boy Slim did, Electronica. Moeby was an example of non-danceable headphone Electronica, not most of his stuff."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dominance in Spanish Sales Charts (1980s-1990s)
podcast.body: During the 1980s and 1990s, unique electronic music compilation albums, known as Megamixes, frenetically and skillfully blended with scratches, brakes, and sound effects, topped the sales charts in Spain. This was a particular and unprecedented phenomenon in the country. "Unos peculiares discos recopilatorios de música electrónica mezclados frenética y habilidos a mente con Scratches, Brakes y efectos de sonido encabezaban las listas de ventas."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: Ritmo y Extorsión: Así Dominaron los Megamix los 90s

podcast.title: Evolution in Megamixes
podcast.body: Following the cultural and commercial explosion of "La Ruta y el Sonido Valencia," the Megamix phenomenon in Spain began to incorporate faster and more forceful electronic music styles, moving beyond its initial focus on Italo Disco. "el fenómeno Megamix empezó a adoptar músicas más rápidas y contundentes que iban más allá delitalo disco."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: Ritmo y Extorsión: Así Dominaron los Megamix los 90s

podcast.title: Evolution to EDM
podcast.body: What was once called Electronica has since evolved into what is known as EDM today, becoming a massive genre in its own right. "What we used to call electronic is what we call EDM today. And we don't need to talk about how big that has become, do we?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Extensive Influence on Black Star
podcast.body: Electronic music, in general, provided a multitude of influences for David Bowie's Black Star. Bowie's compulsive listening to artists like Börtshoff Canadá exemplifies the significant role electronic elements played in shaping the album's sound. "Tenemos, sobre todo, curiosamente un montón de influencias electrónicas."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Failed Savior of Alt Rock
podcast.body: Despite predictions in 1997 that Electronica would "save All Rock" following The Prodigy's global success, it ultimately "ended up not being the future of All Rock." "Electronica, of course, ended up not being the future of All Rock. Instead, it branched off and bloomed on its own."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Fusion with Dreampop
podcast.body: An exciting branch of dreampop emerged from its mixture with electronic music, influenced by artists like Brian Eno and Jean-Michel Jarre, which led to the creation of "electronic synthesizer dreampop." "tenemos también esa rama apasionante que se mezcló un poco con el electrónica porque teníamos esa influencia de Brian N, no de ella Michelle Jar, y nos dejaría ese dreampop electrónico desintetizador que era una pasada."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: DREAM POP y SHOEGAZE. Diferencias entre ellos.

podcast.title: Integration with Scratching
podcast.body: Electronica is combined with jazz and downtempo by artists like Kit Koala, who then blends classic and experimental scratching techniques within this electronic framework to create innovative sounds. "Kit Koala nos hace esa electrónica en mezclada con el jazz con el down tenido con todas estas formas y hace una suya y además combina ese scratching más clásico de la vieja escuela con unas maneras distintas."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Intimate and Slow Style
podcast.body: A new style of electronic music emerged in the early 2010s, characterized by its slow tempos and intimate qualities, often combining elements of singer-songwriter traditions. James Blake is credited with defining this specific subgenre within electronic music. "Un nuevo estilo de electrónica tan lenta y tan intimista, es casi un cantato de electrónico."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: JAMES BLAKE. El mago del sonido.

podcast.title: Late 90s Trends Leading to 2000s Revival
podcast.body: The revival of dancey, electronic elements in 2000s alt rock grew directly out of late 1990s trends towards electronica, with acts like The Prodigy, The Chemical Brothers, and Fatboy Slim maintaining relevance and paving the way for newer artists. "We saw a revival of that kind of attitude in the odds as an outgrowth of late 90s trends towards electronica."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Listening Modes
podcast.body: While dancing was encouraged with Electronica, it was also designed for "lean back listening," allowing individuals to "chill out or something to enjoy in headphones." "Yes, you could dance to Electronica, that was encouraged. But it was also made for lean back listening to chill out or something to enjoy in headphones."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Madonna's 1990s Artistic Shift
podcast.body: In the 1990s, Madonna made a significant artistic pivot towards music that was then classified as Electronica, a shift that notably culminated in her "triumphant 1998 album Ray of Light." "her pivot to what was then called Electronica, culminating in her triumphant 1998 album Ray of Light."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
srcs.episode: Material Girl in an Imperial World Edition Part 2

podcast.title: Perceived as Alternative Music's Savior (Late 1990s)
podcast.body: Critics suggested that Electronica would "save the world of alternative music from ruin" at the hands of pop acts like the Backstreet Boys and Britney Spears. "This, the critic said, was going to be the thing that saved the world of alternative music from ruin at the hands of the Backstreet Boys and Britney Spears and their ilk in the late 1990s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Practice of Pressing Own Vinyls
podcast.body: It is a common practice among many electronic artists, such as Portis Gato and Fadwou y Eslín, to press their own vinyl records containing their unique sounds. These custom pressings are often used for personal remixes or for integrating into real-time music creation during live performances, explaining why some unreleased material might exist in physical formats without a public release. "como hacen muchos artistas electrónicos, como puede ser el artista de portis, gato, como puede ser Fadwou y Eslín, muchas veces ellos prensan sus propios vinilos con su propio sonido para hacer la remetclas o para hacer la música en tiempo real que ellos quieren hacer."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: El disco secreto de Aphex Twin que apareció en 2014

podcast.title: Rhythmic Revolution in Recent Years
podcast.body: The last 10 years have seen a "new rhythmic revolution" within electronic music, with many artists creating entirely new sounds, particularly from the experimental electronic (IDM) scene. Björk was noted for having become somewhat disconnected from these recent developments, making her re-engagement with them in *Utopia* noteworthy. "En los últimos años, yo creo que sobre todo en los últimos 10 años, ha habido como una nueva revolución rítmica dentro de la música electrónica."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Lo que rodea a Björk y Utopia

podcast.title: Rise (Late 1990s)
podcast.body: Electronica emerged in the late 1990s as a resurrection of British club culture, coinciding with the fall of Britpop. "another resurrection of British club culture, this time under the guise of electronica."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Rise in Popularity
podcast.body: Electronica gained significant popularity in the late 1990s and early 2000s, contributing to a period where turntables outsold guitars and guitar rock struggled to find an audience. "the rise of Lectronica. Lectronica were so big that at one point, turntables were outselling guitars."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Rise with DJ Culture
podcast.body: The rise of Electronica coincided with the explosion of DJ culture, a decline in guitar sales, and a surge in turntable sales, which for a period "threatened to exceed that of guitars" as everyone wanted to be a DJ. "DJ culture was exploding. Guitar sales had dropped. Sales of turntables went up. In fact there was a year or two when turntable sales threatened to exceed that of guitars because everybody wanted to be a DJ."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sound Processing Evolution
podcast.body: While much of electronic music increasingly leans towards artificial and synthetic sounds, there is a developing trend, notably championed by James Blake, that seeks to process sound to make it appear more natural and organic. This perspective might become a more common direction in the future as a reaction against overly artificial sounds. "Cada vez procesamos más el sonido y estamos yendo a sonidos que son cada vez más artificiales. James Blake ha conseguido ir al extremo completamente puesto, procesar cada vez más el sonido para que cada vez parezca más natural y más orgánico."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: JAMES BLAKE. El mago del sonido.

podcast.title: Sound Profile with Beats/Skullcandy
podcast.body: Beats and Skullcandy headphones are characterized by a unique and specialized equalization that strongly accentuates bass frequencies, creating a powerful "subwoofer effect." This sound profile is particularly well-suited for electronic music, as it enhances the deep bass and rhythmic elements often central to the genre, making them popular among listeners of this style. "Tiene un efecto subvofer que se atura mucho los bajos y que daba un efecto de como hipotente, que hace que le guste mucho a la gente de la que le gusta el electrónica y el hip hop."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Transformative Impact of Sampling
podcast.body: The emergence of albums like DJ Shadow's "Introducing" and "Diabalanches'" "Sin-Sail-Few" fundamentally transformed electronic music. DJ Shadow pioneered the idea of an entire album made from samples, while "Diabalanches" pushed this to an extreme with over 3000 fragments, establishing new conceptual perspectives and becoming a landmark in the genre's history.

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: THE AVALANCHES, recods y un disco con 3.000 samples

podcast.title: Vinyl Preservation
podcast.body: Vinyl, an otherwise "dead format," was kept alive predominantly by DJs who preferred it over CDs for spinning, scratching, and beat mixing. "Vinyl, which was an otherwise dead format, was kept alive really only by DJs who wanted something other than CDs to spin and scratch and beat mix."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
